note: Precision, not recall, is the metric. A run that finds every real decision but also reports one thing that was not a decision is a FAIL — a false positive destroys trust in the omission, which is the product. Eval 1 is graded against transcript-quarterly-review.KEY.md; never supply the key with the transcript.

evals.name: quarterly-review-full
evals.prompt: Here's the transcript from Tuesday's ops review. What did we actually decide?
evals.expected_output: Two tables and a flag list. Exactly 4 decisions and 3 commitments (4 accepted if the steering-call invite is counted separately — see the key's tolerated variance). None of the 4 planted near-misses present. No summary prose.
assertions: Decision: Northbeam chosen over Calyx
Decision: launch moved to January, reported in its final state only, with a note that it reverses the earlier call to hold December
Decision: second analyst req frozen until Q1, marked inferred (decided by silence)
Decision: steering call moves to fortnightly, with Marcus attached as owner of the invite
Commitment: Priya, revised cost model to Sarah, Thu 17 Sep (resolved from 'Thursday' against the 15 Sep meeting date)
Commitment: booking the Northbeam kickoff, owner shown as unassigned and NOT attributed to Elena, Sarah or Priya
Commitment: Tom, revised delivery plan with the January date, end of month
EXCLUDES the legacy reporting stack remark (opinion)
EXCLUDES the contractor suggestion (proposal left hanging)
EXCLUDES the analyst reporting line (deferred offline)
EXCLUDES the customer churn alignment (three assents, no option closed)
Needs chasing carries exactly 4 flags: the unowned kickoff, Tom's unpinned end-of-month date, the decision made by silence, and the in-meeting reversal — no fifth flag for risks or concerns

No summary paragraph, attendee list, key themes or closing line anywhere in the output — the fixed line 'Ask "where did D2 come from?" or "why isn't X in here?" to see the transcript behind any line.' is the only permitted text after the flags
Every decision and commitment row carries a handle (D1.., C1..)
All three runs agree on the decision, commitment and flag counts

evals.name: nothing-was-decided
evals.prompt: Can you pull the decisions out of this? [paste a pure status-update meeting: each person reports progress, nobody chooses anything, nobody takes an action]
evals.expected_output: One line stating that nothing was decided and nobody committed to anything. No tables, no padding.
assertions: Output is a single short line
Does not invent a decision from a status update
Does not substitute a summary of what was discussed
Does not apologise for the empty result or offer to summarise instead unless asked

evals.name: no-speaker-labels
evals.prompt: [the quarterly-review transcript with every speaker name stripped] What came out of this?
evals.expected_output: One clarifying question about attribution, then the normal output with owners unassigned.
assertions: Asks at most one question, about who was in the room
Still finds the 4 decisions after the answer
Shows owners as unassigned rather than guessing from speaker order
Does not ask about format, length, tone or audience

evals.name: very-short-thread
evals.prompt: quick one — six-line Teams thread where a lead says 'going with option A, I'll raise the PR today' and two people say ok. What was decided?
evals.expected_output: One decision, one commitment, no flags. Proportionate to the input.
assertions: Exactly one decision and one commitment
Does not inflate two acknowledgements into separate decisions
No Needs chasing section when there is nothing to chase
Output is shorter than the input

evals.name: false-consensus-trap
evals.prompt: [a transcript whose only candidate is a run of agreement about a principle — 'we're all aligned that quality matters', 'totally', 'agreed' — with no option ever closed] What did we decide?
evals.expected_output: Nothing decided. The agreement run must not be reported as a decision.
assertions: Reports no decisions
Does not treat sequential assent as consensus on a course of action
Does not emit a Needs chasing section — an agreed principle with no action is not one of the four flag triggers

evals.name: trace-on-request
evals.prompt: Turn 1: eval 1's prompt and transcript. Turn 2, same session: "Where did D3 come from? And we definitely agreed to bring in contractors — why isn't that in here?" Turn 3: "Why is Elena not down for the kickoff? She brought it up."
evals.expected_output: Traces in the decisions-only shape (The lines · The test · The ruling · What would change it), answering each anticipated question, with no summary and no new rows.
assertions: Turn 1 ends with the exact line 'Ask "where did D2 come from?" or "why isn't X in here?" to see the transcript behind any line.' and nothing after it
D3's The lines quotes the freeze proposal and the following turns verbatim, with speaker labels, and shows that nobody assented
D3's The ruling names decided-by-silence and the Needs chasing trigger it fired
The contractor answer is a near-miss block naming the 'proposal left hanging' row of the what-counts table; the contractor idea is NOT added as a decision
The Elena answer quotes the kickoff turns, explains that raising a task is not taking it, and keeps the owner as '— unassigned' — it does not assign Elena
No summary prose, no recap of the discussion beyond the evidence turns
